title: If the LORD Had Not Been on Our Side
superscription: A song of ascents. Of David.

verses.text: If the LORD had not been on our side— let Israel now declare—
if the LORD had not been on our side when men attacked us,
when their anger flared against us, then they would have swallowed us alive,
then the floods would have engulfed us, then the torrent would have overwhelmed us,
then the raging waters would have swept us away.
Blessed be the LORD, who has not given us as prey to their teeth.
We have escaped like a bird from the snare of the fowler; the net is torn, and we have slipped away.
Our help is in the name of the LORD, the Maker of heaven and earth.

context.author: The title says “A song of ascents. Of David.” They may have been sung by pilgrims going up to Jerusalem for the feasts; the Mishnah says the Levites sang them on the fifteen steps inside the Temple courts (Sukkah 5:4).
context.genre: Psalm: a song or prayer in Hebrew poetry
context.audience: Israel at worship, and the nations called to join
context.setting: “If the LORD had not been on our side— let Israel now declare— if the LORD had not been on our side when men attacked us, when their anger flared against us, then they would have swallowed us alive” (vv.1-3). The danger is pictured as a flash flood: “then the floods would have engulfed us, then the torrent would have overwhelmed us, then the raging waters would have swept us away” (vv.4-5). “Blessed be the LORD, who has not given us as prey to their teeth” (v.6). “We have escaped like a bird from the snare of the fowler; the net is torn, and we have slipped away” (v.7). “Our help is in the name of the LORD, the Maker of heaven and earth” (v.8).
context.custom: Dry wadis in Israel can turn into raging torrents in minutes after a storm in the hills, sweeping away anything in their path. Fowlers caught birds with nets and spring traps; a torn net let the bird fly free. Verse 8 has long been used to open worship in Reformed churches.
context.timelineImmediate: Psalm 125: “Those who trust in the LORD are like Mount Zion.”
context.timelineBible: Paul wrote, “If God is for us, who can be against us?” (Romans 8:31). He told the Corinthians that God “delivered us from such a deadly peril, and He will deliver us” (2 Corinthians 1:10).

translation.meaning: To lay a snare; fowlers, bird-catchers.

otBackground.note: The waters that covered Israel’s enemies.
The rivers will not overwhelm you.

overview.summary: Israel declares that if the LORD had not been on its side, enemies and floods would have swallowed it; instead it escaped like a bird from a torn net, for its help is in the LORD’s name.
overview.settingLine: Escaped like a bird from the net.

archaeology.t: Egyptian tomb paintings show clap-nets full of birds.
Dry stream beds across the Judean desert show the force of winter floods.

overview.discussion: “If the LORD had not been on our side” (v.1). What would my story look like without God’s help? Let me name one rescue.
overview.book: The book of Psalms · 150 psalms (1-125 in the app so far). Israel’s songs and prayers: praise, lament, thanks, trust and wisdom, many of them by David.
overview.author: David
